description: Studio S4: founder evidence ledger and provenance-locked narrative on the golden scenarios
label: simulated, based on stated assumptions
disclaimer: Educational planning tool. Not financial, legal or lending advice. Lenders make their own decisions.
scope: Seeded SYNTHETIC founder plans (studio/narrative/golden.py), 6 business types x the SYNTHETIC metro and the real metros in their current local mode. The template narrative passes the grammar and traces by construction (its numbers are typed by the renderer from the ledger); these numbers check that the construction holds on every scenario, they are not evidence about how often a model would write a wrong number.

headline.llm_fallback_rate: not measured: the template provider makes no LLM call; an LLM run (--provider ollama ...) writes results/studio_evidence_metrics_<provider>.json
headline.hf_inference: not measured: the hf_inference provider is disabled by default (UWC_HF_INFERENCE_ENABLED, HF_TOKEN and a verified price are all required) and was never run in this build; the owners decided on no extra spending

checker.note: Both checks read the same mutated sentences. The round-trip audit accepts any number that equals SOME claim of the ledger, so a value moved to another sentence (cross_section) or a flipped comparator is invisible to it by design. The bound check accepts a number only if it equals a claim its own sentence cites through a footnote marker, with the threshold's comparator; cross_section mutations draw values absent from the cited claims, so the bound check's recall there follows from its design. The mutation sentences come from the template narratives the same author wrote, so this is a test of the implementation, not a held-out benchmark.
